reader.requirement: At --std 85, JUST must be accepted wherever JUSTIFIED is, with or without RIGHT, and must mean the same clause. It gets the same right alignment and left truncation (§1985:VI.5.6.4 GR1) and the same refusals: on a group (SR1), on numeric or edited items (SR3), on an index item (SR4), and as a duplicate when both spellings are written.

edition-consulted.switches: word status of JUST / JUSTIFIED (both reserved at 85, the same as 2023)

reader.edition-search: BindEntry sets the single flag justified = true for either token. grep DialectLevel in JustifiedViolation and CheckClauseSubjectsPass's JUSTIFIED arm: none
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers the four spellings' move semantics. The refusals and the duplicate identity are not exercised.

probes.expected: PIC A(4) JUSTIFIED, PIC X9X(2) JUST RIGHT and PIC X(3) JUST right-align short senders with leading spaces and truncate a long sender on the left (§1985:VI.5.6.4 GR1)

probes.printed: COBOL2405 for JUST and JUSTIFIED alike on numeric, numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and index items; COBOL2403 for G1 JUST on a group
probes.expected: the abbreviation is held to SR1, SR3 and SR4 exactly as the full word is

probes.printed: COBOL2423: the clause 'JUST' is written 2 times (PIC X(4) JUST JUSTIFIED)
probes.expected: one clause, so writing both is a duplicate

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.6.3 SR2  (5.6.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2
OK  §1985:VI.5.6.3 SR1  (5.6.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1
OK  §1985:VI.5.6.3 SR4  (5.6.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: justifiedClause is (JUSTIFIED | JUST) RIGHT?, and BindEntry tests only that the node exists, so the two spellings cannot diverge after the parser. The refusal and duplicate probes confirm the spellings are treated as one clause.

refuter.evidence: rju1 (run, --std 85): JUST VALUE "AB" -> [AB   ] and JUSTIFIED RIGHT VALUE "CD" -> [CD   ] (initialization not affected by JUSTIFIED, §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1c); JUST VALUE ALL "XY" -> [XYXYX] and MOVE ALL "PQ" to X(5) JUST -> [PQPQP] (figurative repeated before justification, §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3); JUST in OCCURS -> [   KNOPQ] (left truncation); 77 A(6) JUST -> [   XYZ]; MOVE 9(3) 007 to X(5) JUST -> [  007]; group MOVE over a JUST subordinate not justified -> [ABCD][EF], then [   REF]. rju2: JUST/JUSTIFIED spellings refused identically on every edited/numeric form. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.6.3 SR2; OK §1985:VI.5.6.4 GR1; OK §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1c; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3.
